lessons.title: SELECT: read data from a table
lessons.intro: Five tiny steps. Each one teaches one idea, shows an example, then asks you to try it.

steps.explain: SELECT * FROM a table returns every column and every row.
steps.task: Show every column and row of the products table.
steps.hint: Swap customers for products in the example.

steps.explain: Put a column name after SELECT to get only that column.
steps.task: Show only the name column from products.

steps.explain: List several columns with commas, and they come back in the order you write them.
steps.task: From products, show price first and then name.

steps.explain: You can do maths on a column and name the result with AS.
steps.example: SELECT name, price * 2 AS double_price FROM products;
steps.task: Show each product's name and its price plus 10, in a column called new_price.
steps.solution: SELECT name, price + 10 AS new_price FROM products;

steps.explain: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows, so each value appears once.

lessons.title: WHERE: keep only the rows you need
lessons.intro: Five tiny steps. Each one teaches one idea, shows an example, then asks you to try it.

steps.explain: WHERE keeps only the rows where a condition is true, and text goes in single quotes.
steps.example: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture';
steps.task: Show the names of products in the Stationery category.
steps.solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Stationery';

steps.explain: Numbers need no quotes, and you can compare them with <, >, <= and >=.
steps.example: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price < 20;
steps.task: Show the name and price of products that cost more than 100.
steps.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 100;

steps.explain: AND joins two conditions, and a row stays only if both are true.
steps.example: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' AND price < 50;
steps.task: Show the names of Furniture products that cost less than 100.
steps.solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price < 100;

steps.explain: IN checks whether a value matches any item in a list.
steps.example: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country IN ('UK', 'USA');
steps.task: Show the names of products in the Electronics or Stationery category.
steps.solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category IN ('Electronics', 'Stationery');

steps.explain: A missing value is NULL, and you test for it with IS NULL or IS NOT NULL, never with =.
steps.example: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email IS NULL;
steps.task: Show the names of customers who do have an email address.
steps.solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
